english.title: Vet fail to enter details of veterinary medicinal product administered to a food producing animal in keeper's records
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a veterinary surgeon who had administered a veterinary medicinal product, namely **(..SPECIFY PRODUCT..), to a food-producing animal, failed to enter the details required under regulation 18 of the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..), in the keeper's records or give it to the keeper in writing
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations18, 43(j)and 44(1)of the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013.

english.notes: From the 17th May 2024, this offence no longer applies due to changes made by the Veterinary Medicines (Amendment etc.) Regulations 2024. For the offence applying from this date, see H101686.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
